datasets.name: lmm_crossed
datasets.//: R-only (no jl_formula) by MEASUREMENT, not design: the pinned MixedModels (v5.7.0) wts= is broken for any fit combining a slope block with a second crossed grouping -- on this data it collapses to sigma~3e-5 with beta~[34, 1.2] (initial-objective-evaluation failure, then a degenerate 'optimum'; reproduced under both LN_NEWUOA and LN_BOBYQA, and with a reduced (1+x|g1)+(1|g2) shape). Weighted single-grouping slopes (lmm_slope) and weighted crossed intercepts fit fine. lme4 and glmm agree to 2e-7 here, so the rung stays 2-way gated, same convention as the main harness's sim_binomial_slope_crossed.

datasets.name: sim_sparse_binomial_bigsd
datasets.//: 2-WAY GATE (glmm vs lme4), no jl_formula, by decision rather than by MixedModels limitation: this rung's job is the sparse arm's se_hessian at large theta-hat, and lme4 is the comparator that quantity is calibrated against. MixedModels.jl also throws PosDefException on rung 45, the dense large-theta rung, so a Julia leg in the same theta-hat band would most likely just crash. Same convention as rungs 23/24 and 36: absent jl_formula means engines/mixedmodels.jl skips the rung. Seven crossed intercept-only extras is what routes this to the sparse solver (over MAX_EXTRA_GROUPINGS); every RE block is scalar on purpose, because engines/lme4.R emits stddev_se only for all-scalar binomial/poisson fits and stddev_se is half of what this rung gates. Bernoulli, not Poisson: a Poisson design in this regime pushes counts into the tens of thousands, where the deviance-sum rounding noise dominates the FD Hessian's step independent of any solver tuning (see prep/gen_large_theta_data.R block R4 for the measurement); a Bernoulli response bounds the working weight and removes that noise floor. Sparse-large-theta-hat Poisson coverage is deliberately not attempted for this reason, not a gap left open.

datasets.name: InstEval
datasets.r_formula: y ~ service * dept + studage + lectage + (1 | d) + (1 | s)
datasets.jl_formula: @formula(y ~ 1 + service * dept + studage + lectage + (1 | d) + (1 | s))
datasets.//: TIMING ONLY, not a curated correctness rung: the standard lme4-paper InstEval model (73421 rows, crossed student/instructor intercepts, 2972/1128 levels) used here purely to time glmm's Cholesky/Schur path on a large crossed design, per Bates/Alday/Kokandakar arXiv:2505.11674's term-order fill-in benchmark. No oracle JSON is generated for it by a normal run; it only joins compare.R's comparison if --oracles is run against it explicitly.

datasets.name: sim_probit_large
datasets.//: The corpus's LARGE probit rung. Bernoulli, scalar (1|g), 100 groups x 96 rows = 9600 rows, p = 5, fitted theta-hat ~0.66. cbpp_probit (rung 22) is the only other probit fit anywhere in the suite and is 56 rows at ~3 ms, where a vectorized family kernel is pure measurement noise -- so probit SPEED, and any accuracy drift that needs a long row loop to accumulate, were both invisible before this rung. 96 rows per cluster is deliberate: it puts every conditional mode in the well-determined regime where Laplace is accurate, so a gate miss here means a kernel defect rather than the approximation's own bias (rungs 44-46 own the hard-cell axis). The row count sits under lme4's check.conv.nobsmax = 10000 ceiling, above which glmer stops computing the optimizer Hessian and engines/lme4.R's vcov(use.hessian = TRUE) hard-errors -- that ceiling, not taste, is what caps the rung. Data from prep/gen_probit_large_data.R, which carries the full sizing and coefficient rationale.

datasets.name: sim_cloglog_nested_crossed
datasets.//: 2-WAY GATE (glmm vs lme4), no jl_formula: engines/mixedmodels.jl's binomial-link dispatch only builds LogitLink/ProbitLink and errors on any other link string, so a cloglog leg there would abort the whole --oracles run, same reason rungs 23/24/36/46 stay 2-way. Rung 21 (sim_nested_crossed_mix)'s design (g1/g2 nested, c1 crossed) with a cloglog Bernoulli response in place of the gaussian one -- the one non-canonical link paired with a structured-extras shape that combines a nested and a crossed grouping in the same model, on the bit-identity tripwire from here on.

//large_theta_rungs: Rungs 44-46 + the two sim_binomial_bigsd_agq_k* goldens: the large-theta-hat regime. Rung 44 sim_binomial_bigsd is Bernoulli, scalar (1|g), 300 groups x 6 obs, fitted theta-hat 4.5106 -- 3.4x the corpus's previous GLMM maximum (1.339, VerbAgg); rung 45 sim_poisson_bigsd is the count-family counterpart at 2.9716. Both are Laplace (nAGQ=1) curated rungs on the EXISTING tiers, not a new tier and not an expansion of the curated 6-rung cross-engine oracle (design 6). Rung 46 sim_sparse_binomial_bigsd is the SPARSE arm of the same regime -- one primary grouping g1 (300 groups x 12) plus seven crossed intercept-only extras c1-c7, fitted theta-hat(g1) 3.9076 -- added because rungs 44-45 are both dense-routed scalar (1|g), so the sparse solver's large-theta-hat behavior was untested rather than merely uncalibrated; it is a 2-way gate (glmm vs lme4 only, see its own '//' comment above for why). Their data comes from prep/gen_large_theta_data.R, the third of the five prep scripts (export_data.R rungs 1-28, gen_weights_data.R 29-43, gen_illcond_data.R, gen_scale_data.R). THE THIRD DATASET OF THAT SPEC, sim_binomial_zerosd (theta = 0 exactly), IS DELIBERATELY NOT A RUNG: lme4's vcov(m, use.hessian = TRUE) HARD-ERRORS on a boundary fit ('Hessian is unavailable' -- m@optinfo$derivs is NULL), which is exactly what engines/lme4.R:269 and :146 call, so adding it as a curated rung would abort the whole oracle run. What it exists to gate is a FLAG divergence, not a number -- lme4 warns 'boundary (singular) fit' (so engines/lme4.R records converged = FALSE) while glmm pins the component and reports converged = true with singular = true, and BOTH land on a bit-exact 0.0 stddev, so compare.R's numeric gates would see nothing. It is gated in-crate instead, by glmm_zerosd_boundary_reports_converged_and_singular in src/fit/glmm_tests.rs, which needs no oracle JSON. Verified 2026-07-30 that rel_max(0.0, 0.0) = 0 on this dataset, i.e. the two engines do not straddle rel_max's 1e-12 denominator floor.
//gamma_rungs: Rung 23 (sim_gamma, dense): varcorr is on the sigma-hat^2 scale. Rung 24 (sim_sparse_gamma) is a curated rung as of 2026-07-21. The frontend lowers random effects in FORMULA ORDER (nested terms still sort first -- NestedWithin is relative to the primary): for (1|gp)+(1+x1..x4|ge), gp is primary, the model routes SPARSE, and it lands 2e-4 above lme4 -- matching the in-crate golden that hand-builds the same orientation, without relaxing tolerances. If ge were primary instead (q_p=5, e.g. by writing the slope term first), the model would route DENSE, whose joint optimizer lands ~2e-3 deviance above the tolPwrss=1e-13 lme4 optimum (beta[0] 1.9e-2 off); that dense joint optimizer shortfall on a q_p=5 primary with an extra grouping is real and unresolved (dense stage-1/2 schedule work is a separate item), but FORMULA ORDER keeps rung 24 off that path. These are rung-18-style 2-WAY gates (no jl_formula): MixedModels' Gamma GLMM is a documented different estimator, its JSONs stay intentionally absent. See validation/README.md. GAMMA-INVERSE WITH RANDOM EFFECTS, SPARSE: no oracle is obtainable for spec sim_sparse_gamma_inv over the sim_sparse_gamma data (checked 2026-07-21), so it is not a rung. That data is simulated under a LOG link and spans y 0.0045..265, so an inverse-link model is misspecified for it: eta goes negative, mu = 1/eta with it, and the Gamma likelihood is undefined. lme4 dies with 'PIRLS loop resulted in NaN value', and so does a plain fixed-only stats::glm on the same formula -- the failure is the data, not the mixed solver. Oracling this cell needs a dataset simulated under the inverse link, which is a new simulated fixture and a separate decision. The DENSE Gamma-inverse mixed cell is covered: sim_gamma_inv_glmm fits cleanly on sim_gamma.
//agq_field: `agq: <k>` marks the datasets AGQ can be run on, for the OPT-IN timing pass only (VALIDATION_AGQ, read by engines/lme4.R and engines/glmm.rs). It is inert on a normal run: the curated cross-engine sweep stays pinned at nAGQ=1 (engines/lme4.R's fit_call) and the AGQ pass writes to results/{lme4,glmm}_agq_*, which compare.R's results/lme4_{empirical,simulated}/*.json glob never sees -- design 6, 'the curated 6-rung oracle is NOT expanded'. Eligibility is glmm's AGQ gate (src/glmm/deviance.rs): binomial/Poisson, ONE grouping factor, q <= 3. Arabidopsis and sim_poisson_nested are excluded for having two groupings. The three vector-RE entries (sim_binomial_slope1/sim_poisson_slope1 q=2, sim_binomial_slope2 q=3) are glmm-only -- glmer refuses nAGQ>1 for vector REs, so lme4.R skips them and their rows carry no lme4 time.
//m3_goldens: Family/link/AGQ reference fits for the IN-CRATE frozen goldens (NOT curated rungs). Generated by engines/goldens_agq.R into validation/goldens/<name>.json -- a SEPARATE dir so compare.R's results/<engine>/*.json glob (the curated cross-engine sweep) is untouched, per design 6 'the curated 6-rung oracle is NOT expanded'. lme4/MASS only; no Julia/Rust cross-check. Every golden in goldens/ must have an entry here and therefore a generator -- sleepstudy_lmm, penicillin_lmm and pastes_lmm are registered and regenerable as of 2026-07-21; they are the SAME datasets as rungs 2/3/4 but distinct model specs (pastes_lmm is the nested (1|batch/cask) form, rung 4 is the flat idiom), which is why they are separate goldens rather than rung results. All three are byte-reproducible from this script (nagq field, 12-sig-fig rounding, pastes_lmm's varcomp blocks keyed and ordered by group name to match the cask:batch-first order lme4's VarCorr emits): regenerating them reproduces every estimate (penicillin stddev to 6e-7, the rounding; pastes to 1e-7 once the two blocks are matched by name). Reproducing them requires every multi-block varcomp read in the crate to key by group NAME rather than index: glmm emits declaration order, lme4's VarCorr emits descending level count, and pastes_lmm is the fixture where the two disagree.

m3_goldens.name: sim_cloglog_glm
m3_goldens.//: Reuses rung 48's data (sim_probit_large, 9600 Bernoulli rows) rather than a new fixture: no domain hazard fitting cloglog on probit-simulated data (mu stays in (0,1) for every eta), and it is the only large binomial fixture in the corpus.

m3_goldens.name: sim_igauss_glm
m3_goldens.//: The corpus's only inverse-Gaussian fixture (prep/gen_igauss_data.R, which carries the sizing rationale), and GLM-only by design: the family's mixed-model path is not built (fit faults at the model-shape gate), so no glmm cell and no jl_formula (MixedModels.jl has no fixed-only inverse-Gaussian GLM path). Paired with sim_igauss_inv_sq_glm below on the same data -- link 'log' and link '1/mu^2' -- mirroring sim_gamma_glm / sim_gamma_inv_glm, because inverse-Gaussian data is link-agnostic the same way Gamma data is: any y > 0 fits under both.

//weights_tier: WEIGHTS validation suite, fit by the same engines/compare as every other rung. Conventions on top of the main manifest: `weights_col` names a plain per-row prior-weight CSV column (mutually exclusive with the aggregated-binomial `weights` field); rungs WITHOUT a jl_formula are lme4-only (fixed-only models MixedModels cannot fit, or R-only pathologicals) and fit.jl skips them; `gate` marks the two fit-time special gates (dropped_rows in fit.R, unit_identity in fit.rs).
//inference_references: Inference reference JSONs (lmerTest tests, RLRT, ANOVA tables) for the inference layer. One tree, goldens/inference/{lmertest,rlrt,anova}/<name>.json, and this one block; an entry's `kind` (lmertest, rlrt or anova) picks its directory. Entry fields: `name`; `kind`; `data`, the CSV path relative to validation/ (e.g. data/simulated/lmm_intercept.csv, data/empirical/Dyestuff2.csv; a rung dataset is cited by its CSV path, not by its `datasets` name), or null for a fit-free entry, one with no model fit, whose `r_formula` is null too; `r_formula`; optional `factors`, the `data` columns read as factors (as an `m3_goldens` entry's `factors`; each must be a column of the CSV; absent means none); `generator`, the bare file name of the script under tools/ that writes the JSON (e.g. goldens_rlrt.R, not a path; it sources tools/inference_common.R); optional `pending_reference`, a non-empty reason, set while the JSON does not exist yet (generate it with VALIDATION_ONLY=<name> and drop the field in the same change); any further field is kind-specific and owned by the generator that reads it. These are never rows in `datasets` (nor in `m3_goldens`), so the curated sweep, the bit-identity dump and goldens_agq.R see nothing new. Names are unique across kinds and disjoint from the `datasets` and `m3_goldens` names. Checked by tests/inference_references.rs.
